Phase 8 is too large for one turn, so I split it. Phases 9 and 10 keep their numbers, so “OpenStreetMap after phase 9” still holds.

Sub-phase	Scope	Status
8a	GPS map panel in Compose	Written, not delivered
8b	Trail and measure map panels	Next
8c	Remaining dialogs, single activity with Navigation Compose, drop AppCompat themes	Planned
What 8a contains:

GPS panel rewritten: the fragment now only hosts a Compose screen. The toolbar, map tools, info sheet and speedometer are all Compose. The info sheet is a Material 3 bottom sheet in portrait and a side column in landscape.
Map lifecycle shared: a new MapLifecycle observer drives the map view, and the map search screen now uses it too. I removed the old early onResume() call from CustomMaps.onCreate.
Address lookups: they used to run a blocking geocoder call on every location fix. Now they use the non-blocking geocoder on Android 13+ and only run after the position moves at least 25 m, which should help battery.
Save location fix: saving now uses the shared database instance instead of opening a second one.
Navigate: if Google Maps isn’t installed, it now falls back to a generic geo: link.
Volume-key zoom: now handled through Compose key events.
New tests: GeoDistanceTest and SpeedometerDialTest.
README: the phase table is updated.
Deleted:
The old toolbar, tools, speedometer and popup classes.
10 GPS layouts.
The Speedometer styleable.
Three unused PaddingAware* views.
The ripple drawable.
The unused info_error string and info_text_item_line_spacing dimen, across all locales.
Reply “continue” and I’ll redo this, check it again, and deliver it as a tar.gz with one git rm command. As before, I can’t compile here, so CI is the real check.

On the OpenStreetMap fallback: no API key is needed. osmdroid with the standard OSM tiles works without one and caches viewed tiles on the device automatically. The catch is OSM’s tile usage policy. It requires a proper User-Agent (the app ID) and forbids bulk pre-downloading of areas, so “cache what you’ve looked at” is fine but “download this whole region for offline use” is not. Most vector-tile providers (MapTiler, Stadia) do need keys; OpenFreeMap is a keyless vector option if we want one later. My plan is to put the map behind a small interface during 8b, so swapping in osmdroid in phase 10 is a contained change.

Presented file
The archive is positional-phase8a.tar.gz. It contains the crash fix and the GPS panel from phase 8a. Extract it at the repo root; it holds only new and changed files.

Cause of the crash: the phase 7 Clock screen loaded the clock’s sweep trail through Compose’s image loader. That trail image is an XML shape, and Compose can only load vector images and bitmaps, so it throws as soon as the Clock panel is drawn. The app reopens on the last panel you used, so once you had opened Clock, every launch crashed. The time zone picker had the same problem with its “selected” dot (an XML layer-list), so it would also crash whenever a selected zone was on screen.

Fixes:

The sweep trail is now drawn directly with a sweep gradient.
The selected time zone dot is now a plain filled circle.
A new unit test, ComposeDrawablesTest, fails the build if any image drawn by Compose isn’t a vector or bitmap.
Other checks I made:

Every class name in a layout or the manifest points to a class that exists.
The phase 6 database changes are consistent with the stored schemas.
Rounding, list keys, sensor setup and the clock and sky calculations hold up.
Nothing else turned up that would crash at launch. I still can’t build or run the app here, so CI and your phone are the real test. If it still crashes, a stack trace from adb logcat would let me pin it down.

Phase 8a, delivered here:

The GPS panel is now Compose, as described last time.
The map follows the screen’s lifecycle through a shared observer.
Address lookups use the non-blocking geocoder on Android 13+ and run only after you move 25 m.
Saving a location reuses the shared database.
New tests: GeoDistanceTest and SpeedometerDialTest.
The README is updated.

Presented file
Phase 8b is in positional-phase8b.tar.gz: extract it at the repo root; it contains only changed and new files. I couldn’t compile it here (no Android SDK), so CI is the real check; the 8a build passed CI.

Panels

Shared map layout: a new MapPanel.kt now holds the map layout, toolbar, tool buttons and sheet handle used by all three map panels. The GPS screen was rebuilt on it without changing what it does.
Trail panel: now in Compose. The list of trail points opens as a bottom sheet in portrait and sits beside the map in landscape. Long-pressing a point gives navigate, share, copy and delete. Choosing a marker icon is now a small grid dialog instead of the old popup window.
Measure panel: now in Compose. The name, point count and distances show in a card at the bottom. That card sits above the bottom bar, so the old code that tracked the bar’s size is gone.
Data and bug fixes

Trail points update live: they now come from Room as a Flow. Previously every load, save and delete opened and closed its own database. Now one database stays open for the current trail, and it is closed before that trail is deleted.
Crash on Android 7–10 fixed: TrailPoint’s name and note getters used a Java method that only exists from Android 11. Phone or emulator testing on those versions would have crashed on the trail panel.
Distances: one shared DistanceText formatter now handles trail, measure and direction distances. Direction used to switch from feet to miles at 1000 m; all three now switch at one mile.
Navigation links: navigate and share go through a shared MapIntents helper. If Google Maps isn’t installed, it falls back to a generic geo: link.
Bottom bar callback: the panels now tell MainActivity to show or hide the bar through a new BottomBarHost interface, replacing BottomSheetSlide.
Cleanup

The timeline list library is removed from build.gradle.
Strings and dimensions that nothing uses any more are removed from every language.
New tests: DistanceTextTest, and a path-length test added to GeoDistanceTest.
The README is updated.

Presented file
Phase 8b is in positional-phase8b.tar.gz: extract it at the repo root; it contains only changed and new files. I couldn’t compile it here (no Android SDK), so CI is the real check; the 8a build passed CI.

Panels

Shared map layout: a new MapPanel.kt now holds the map layout, toolbar, tool buttons and sheet handle used by all three map panels. The GPS screen was rebuilt on it without changing what it does.
Trail panel: now in Compose. The list of trail points opens as a bottom sheet in portrait and sits beside the map in landscape. Long-pressing a point gives navigate, share, copy and delete. Choosing a marker icon is now a small grid dialog instead of the old popup window.
Measure panel: now in Compose. The name, point count and distances show in a card at the bottom. That card sits above the bottom bar, so the old code that tracked the bar’s size is gone.
Data and bug fixes

Trail points update live: they now come from Room as a Flow. Previously every load, save and delete opened and closed its own database. Now one database stays open for the current trail, and it is closed before that trail is deleted.
Crash on Android 7–10 fixed: TrailPoint’s name and note getters used a Java method that only exists from Android 11. Phone or emulator testing on those versions would have crashed on the trail panel.
Distances: one shared DistanceText formatter now handles trail, measure and direction distances. Direction used to switch from feet to miles at 1000 m; all three now switch at one mile.
Navigation links: navigate and share go through a shared MapIntents helper. If Google Maps isn’t installed, it falls back to a generic geo: link.
Bottom bar callback: the panels now tell MainActivity to show or hide the bar through a new BottomBarHost interface, replacing BottomSheetSlide.
Cleanup

The timeline list library is removed from build.gradle.
Strings and dimensions that nothing uses any more are removed from every language.
New tests: DistanceTextTest, and a path-length test added to GeoDistanceTest.
The README is updated.

I fixed the failing build and finished part of phase 8c: the six panel menus are now Compose. The rest of 8c was too large for one pass, so I split it in the README. 8d is the remaining dialogs and is next; 8e is the single activity with Navigation Compose and dropping the AppCompat themes. Phases 9 and 10 keep their numbers.

The build failure was my mistake in 8b. BottomBarItems.java read Measure.TAG, which I removed when I rewrote the Measure panel. It is now the literal "Measure", so the saved “last open panel” value is unchanged. In that CI run both Kotlin compiles passed before the Java error. The 8b and 8c Compose code is still unverified until CI runs, and the unit tests and lint check had not run yet. I still can’t build here, so CI is the real check.

Panel menus: the GPS, trail, measure, compass, clock and direction menus are now one Compose bottom sheet. A new PanelMenus.kt lists each panel’s switches and actions, and MenuSheet.kt shows them. When satellite mode is on, the buildings and high-contrast switches are greyed out as before. The six old menu dialogs and their layouts are deleted.

Other fixes:

Rotation crash: four sub-dialogs (clock needles, clock motion type, compass bloom skins, compass physical properties) reopened their menu while being destroyed. Rotating the phone with one open could crash with “Can not perform this action after onSaveInstanceState”. The pin customization dialog did the same with the GPS menu. All five no longer do this.
Measure.java:
getMeasurePoints() was marked as never returning null but could return null, which could crash the Kotlin code that uses it. It now returns an empty list instead.
Room’s warning about choosing between several constructors is gone.
I left the database column itself unchanged, because changing it would wipe saved measures.
Cleanup: the unused unnecessary-null-check warnings are tidied. Fifteen unused icons, one unused view class and one dimension are removed.
New test: MenuSheetStateTest.
README is updated.

Phase 8d:

Dialog host: a new DialogHost holds the panel dialogs, and the panels’ Compose views draw it alongside the panel menus.
Error dialogs: the sensor error and Play-services error are now a Compose MessageDialog.
Clock motion type: it now uses the existing Compose choice dialog.
New measure / new trail: both reuse the Compose name-and-note dialog. New trail still remembers an unfinished name and note between openings and rejects duplicate trail names.
New marker: same dialog, now with an inline row of marker icons. This replaces the popup marker grid.
Deleted: 5 dialog fragments, the marker popup and its adapter, 2 unused view classes, 7 layouts, 2 animations, 1 style and 1 colour.
New test: DialogHostTest.
README: updated. What’s left of phase 8 is now 8e, the remaining dialogs, which is next. The single activity with Navigation Compose and dropping the AppCompat themes moved to 8f.

I fixed the failing build and finished part of phase 8c: the six panel menus are now Compose. The rest of 8c was too large for one pass, so I split it in the README. 8d is the remaining dialogs and is next; 8e is the single activity with Navigation Compose and dropping the AppCompat themes. Phases 9 and 10 keep their numbers.

The build failure was my mistake in 8b. BottomBarItems.java read Measure.TAG, which I removed when I rewrote the Measure panel. It is now the literal "Measure", so the saved “last open panel” value is unchanged. In that CI run both Kotlin compiles passed before the Java error. The 8b and 8c Compose code is still unverified until CI runs, and the unit tests and lint check had not run yet. I still can’t build here, so CI is the real check.

Panel menus: the GPS, trail, measure, compass, clock and direction menus are now one Compose bottom sheet. A new PanelMenus.kt lists each panel’s switches and actions, and MenuSheet.kt shows them. When satellite mode is on, the buildings and high-contrast switches are greyed out as before. The six old menu dialogs and their layouts are deleted.

Other fixes:

Rotation crash: four sub-dialogs (clock needles, clock motion type, compass bloom skins, compass physical properties) reopened their menu while being destroyed. Rotating the phone with one open could crash with “Can not perform this action after onSaveInstanceState”. The pin customization dialog did the same with the GPS menu. All five no longer do this.
Measure.java:
getMeasurePoints() was marked as never returning null but could return null, which could crash the Kotlin code that uses it. It now returns an empty list instead.
Room’s warning about choosing between several constructors is gone.
I left the database column itself unchanged, because changing it would wipe saved measures.
Cleanup: the unused unnecessary-null-check warnings are tidied. Fifteen unused icons, one unused view class and one dimension are removed.
New test: MenuSheetStateTest.

Dialogs now in Compose:

Clock needle and bloom skin pickers: swipe pages with a “3/10”-style counter; the choice saves when the swipe settles.
Pin customization: pin pager, size and opacity sliders, and a reset button.
Compass physical properties: an on/off switch, three sliders, reset and help. As before, a slider at 0 saves 0.1.

Phase 8f is in positional-phase8f.tar.gz; extract it at the repo root. It contains only changed and new files. The build from your last push (8e) passed CI. I can’t compile here, so the next CI run is the real check for 8f.

Dialogs now in Compose:

Location summary (the GPS toolbar pin button and the clock panel’s location button): time zone, latitude, longitude and address, with a share button. Share uses the same text as the GPS panel’s share, now in one shared helper.
Location details: accuracy and altitude history drawn as Compose line charts, with min, max and average in metres or feet.
Coordinate formats: degrees-minutes-seconds, degrees-minutes, decimal degrees, MGRS and UTM, with a copy button.
Battery fix: the location view model was computing all five coordinate formats, including MGRS and UTM, on every GPS fix even when nothing showed them. They are now computed only while the coordinate dialog is open. The accuracy and altitude history lists are also handed out as copies, so the UI never reads a list while it is being changed.

Removed:

The three dialog fragments and their layouts.
The old sparkline chart package.
The fast-scroller package, the custom list view and its list-row helper. Nothing used them after this change.
Two unused view classes.
The dynamicanimation dependency.
Unused styles, styleables, dimensions and strings, in every language.
TextViewUtils is cut down to the one function still used.
New tests: SeriesStatsTest and LocationShareTest.

README: updated. The panel switcher moves to 8g, together with the single activity and dropping the AppCompat themes. It lives in MainActivity, which 8g replaces.

Phase 8f is in positional-phase8f.tar.gz; extract it at the repo root. It contains only changed and new files. The build from your last push (8e) passed CI. I can’t compile here, so the next CI run is the real check for 8f.

Dialogs now in Compose:

Location summary (the GPS toolbar pin button and the clock panel’s location button): time zone, latitude, longitude and address, with a share button. Share uses the same text as the GPS panel’s share, now in one shared helper.
Location details: accuracy and altitude history drawn as Compose line charts, with min, max and average in metres or feet.
Coordinate formats: degrees-minutes-seconds, degrees-minutes, decimal degrees, MGRS and UTM, with a copy button.
Battery fix: the location view model was computing all five coordinate formats, including MGRS and UTM, on every GPS fix even when nothing showed them. They are now computed only while the coordinate dialog is open. The accuracy and altitude history lists are also handed out as copies, so the UI never reads a list while it is being changed.

Removed:

The three dialog fragments and their layouts.
The old sparkline chart package.
The fast-scroller package, the custom list view and its list-row helper. Nothing used them after this change.
Two unused view classes.
The dynamicanimation dependency.
Unused styles, styleables, dimensions and strings, in every language.
TextViewUtils is cut down to the one function still used.
New tests: SeriesStatsTest and LocationShareTest.

README: updated. The panel switcher moves to 8g, together with the single activity and dropping the AppCompat themes. It lives in MainActivity, which 8g replaces.

Phase 8g is in positional-phase8g.tar.gz; extract it at the repo root. It contains only changed and new files. The build from your last push (8f) passed CI. I can’t compile here, so the next CI run is the real check for 8g.

Main screen is now Compose:

Panel hosting: MainActivity shows the current panel with AndroidFragment, so the existing panel fragments keep working unchanged. This needs a new dependency, androidx.fragment:fragment-compose. I set it to 1.9.1 to match fragment-ktx, but could not confirm that version exists, so CI will be the first check. The old view-pager bottom bar, its layout and the panel transition animation are gone.
Panel switcher: a floating accent button at the bottom right replaces the old bottom bar.
Tapping it opens a grid of all eight panels, each in its own colour.
Swiping up or down on it steps to the next or previous panel.
The panel name shows next to the button for about a second after each change.
Map panels still hide it in full screen.
Saved panel: saved by tag only, so the panel you last used still opens after the update. Home-screen shortcuts still work. Unknown or old values fall back to the GPS panel.
Location permission: now requested through the Activity Result API instead of the deprecated callback.
Location service: start, stop and switching between the Android and fused location sources share one small helper.
Removed:

The bottom-bar adapter, item list and model, the panel dialog and its adapter, and their callback interfaces.
The page transformer, three rounded-corner and ripple layout classes, the layout background helper, the base bottom-sheet dialog and the old view helpers.
The unused bottom-bar visibility preferences, since nothing read them.
Four layouts, four animations, the bottom-sheet and dialog styles, the rounded-corner styleable and unused dimensions.
The recyclerview dependency.
New test: PanelCatalogTest (unknown tags fall back to GPS, swiping wraps around, tags are unique).

README: updated. 8h is next: panels become plain Compose screens with Navigation Compose, the sub screens join the same navigation graph, and fragments and the AppCompat themes go away.

Ran 21 commands, shared files
Phase 8h is in positional-phase8h.tar.gz; extract it at the repo root. It contains only changed and new files. The build from your last push (8g) passed CI. I can’t compile here, so the next CI run is the real check for 8h.

Panels are no longer fragments. Each panel is now a plain class built on a new PanelController base (in extensions/panel/).

Lifecycle: each panel has its own lifecycle that follows the activity while the panel is on screen. When you switch panels, that lifecycle is destroyed. Sensors, map views, location observers and coroutines are already tied to it, so they all stop cleanly without per-panel cleanup code.
Shared plumbing: the base class holds what every panel used to set up itself: menus, dialogs, string lookups, starting activities, settings-change listening, and results from other screens (search and permission requests).
SensorPanel moved to the new package and builds on the same base.
MainActivity creates the selected panel directly, so the fragment-compose dependency is gone again.
Settings screen: now takes the top inset in dp directly.
Behaviour change: panels no longer save the map camera or full-screen state across rotation. Each rotation rebuilds the panel, and the map starts from your saved zoom and position as it does on a normal open. The full-screen home-screen shortcut still works.

No new tests. The lifecycle classes need Android’s main thread, which plain JVM unit tests don’t provide.

README: updated, including the project layout. 8i is next: the sub screens and splash move into the single activity with Navigation Compose, and the remaining fragment use and the AppCompat themes go away.
